calls.head: Strength in numbers for the Bruins
calls.body: The Bruins roll four lines, but the Jets lean on their top six. Boston is one of the league’s best for depth, and Winnipeg is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. If this one comes down to the bottom six, that suits the Bruins.

surprises.head: Winnipeg’s power play came alive
surprises.body: Winnipeg’s power play created 19.6 expected goals per 60, against their usual 7.2 and a league average of 7.7. A team strays this far about once every 100 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

story.head: Peterka ends it in overtime
paras: The Jets’ Tyrel Bauer and the Jets’ Viggo Björck both played their first NHL game. Mario Ferraro made his Jets debut, after seven seasons with the Sharks. Dylan DeMelo got the scoring started for the Jets early in the first, and Mark Kastelic and Bauer dropped the gloves midway through the period. Hampus Lindholm tied it 1-1 for Boston later in the period. James Hagens, in his fourth NHL game, scored his first NHL goal, set up by Nikita Zadorov, late in the period to put the Bruins ahead 2-1. Kyle Connor tied it up for Winnipeg on the power play early in the second, and Ferraro put the Jets up 3-2 with just eight seconds left in the period. With the goalie pulled and less than two minutes left, Elias Lindholm tied it up for Boston. JJ Peterka won it in overtime.
The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. Jeremy Swayman made 30 saves for the Bruins, and Stuart Skinner stopped 26 of 30.
The Jets hit a post and the crossbar and came up a goal short. The Bruins moved to 2-0-0, tied for first in the NHL in points. The Jets dropped to 0-0-1 but climbed out of last place in the NHL.

items.text: The Jets opened their season with a loss at home.
